structuring-and-managing-special-purpose.title: Structuring and Managing a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for PPP
structuring-and-managing-special-purpose.summary: Practical executive training on structuring, financing, governing, and managing Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) for bankable Public-Private Partnership (PPP) infrastructure and energy projects.
structuring-and-managing-special-purpose.content:
OVERVIEW

The energy sector in Kenya is undergoing significant transformation driven by increasing demand for reliable electricity, the transition towards renewable energy, and the need for sustainable financing models to support infrastructure development. As the national power utility, Kenya Power and Lighting Company (KPLC) plays a central role in electricity distribution and in facilitating investments that enhance grid stability, expansion, and efficiency.

In response to fiscal constraints and the growing need for private sector participation, Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) have emerged as a critical mechanism for financing and delivering energy infrastructure projects. Within this framework, the use of Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) has become a standard approach for structuring PPP projects, enabling risk sharing, ring-fencing of assets, and efficient project financing.

SPVs serve as legally independent entities established specifically to design, finance, build, operate, and manage infrastructure projects. In PPP arrangements, they provide a structured platform through which public and private partners can allocate risks, mobilize capital, and ensure accountability and transparency in project execution. However, the effective structuring and management of SPVs requires a strong understanding of financial engineering, legal frameworks, governance structures, and risk management mechanisms.

Despite the growing adoption of PPPs in the energy sector, there remain capacity gaps in the design, negotiation, and operational management of SPVs. These challenges are further compounded by evolving regulatory requirements, complex financing arrangements, and the need to align projects with national energy policies and sustainability goals. Additionally, the increasing integration of renewable energy projects, grid modernization initiatives, and regional power trade requires more sophisticated approaches to project structuring and management.

Globally, best practices in PPP implementation emphasize the importance of well-structured SPVs to ensure bankability, investor confidence, and long-term project viability. For institutions such as Kenya Power and Lighting Company, strengthening internal capacity in SPV structuring and management is essential to effectively engage with private sector partners, manage contractual obligations, and optimize project outcomes.

Against this backdrop, this training programme is designed to equip participants with contemporary knowledge and practical skills in structuring, financing, and managing Special Purpose Vehicles within PPP frameworks. It aims to enhance the capacity of KPLC staff to navigate complex PPP arrangements, improve project performance, and contribute to the sustainable development of the energy sector.

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

OVERALL OBJECTIVE

To equip participants with the knowledge and practical skills required to structure, finance, govern, and manage Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) for effective implementation of Public-Private Partnership (PPP) projects in the energy sector.

SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES

By the end of the programme, participants will be able to:

  • Understand the PPP framework and lifecycle in infrastructure development
  • Design and structure bankable SPVs for energy projects
  • Analyze and allocate project risks effectively
  • Develop appropriate financial models and funding structures
  • Strengthen governance, compliance, and oversight mechanisms for SPVs
  • Manage contracts, stakeholders, and performance within PPP arrangements
  • Apply best practices in SPV management to enhance project sustainability

COURSE OUTLINE

Day 1: Foundations of PPPs and SPVs

Module 1: Introduction to PPP Frameworks

  • Overview of PPP concepts and models (BOT, BOOT, DBFO, etc.)
  • PPP policy and regulatory environment in Kenya
  • Role of public institutions and private sector partners

Module 2: Fundamentals of Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs)

  • Definition, purpose, and characteristics of SPVs
  • Legal and institutional structures of SPVs
  • Role of SPVs in PPP project delivery

Module 3: PPP Project Lifecycle

  • Project identification, preparation, procurement, and implementation
  • Integration of SPVs across the project lifecycle

Day 2: Structuring SPVs for PPP Projects

Module 4: Legal and Institutional Structuring

  • SPV registration, ownership, and shareholding structures
  • Shareholder agreements and governance frameworks
  • Regulatory compliance requirements

Module 5: Risk Allocation and Mitigation

  • Identification of project risks (financial, operational, regulatory, political)
  • Risk allocation between public and private partners
  • Risk mitigation instruments (guarantees, insurance, etc.)

Module 6: Contractual Frameworks

  • Key PPP agreements (concession agreements, PPAs, EPC contracts)
  • Roles and obligations of parties
  • Dispute resolution mechanisms

Day 3: Financial Structuring and Bankability

Module 7: Financial Modelling and Project Finance

  • Principles of project finance
  • SPV financial structure (equity, debt, hybrid instruments)
  • Financial modelling basics

Module 8: Funding and Investment Structures

  • Sources of financing (DFIs, commercial banks, capital markets)
  • Blended finance and public funding support
  • Investor expectations and bankability criteria

Module 9: Financial Risk Management

  • Currency risk, interest rate risk, and liquidity risk
  • Revenue models and tariff structures
  • Financial sustainability strategies

Day 4: Governance, Operations, and Performance Management

Module 10: SPV Governance and Oversight

  • Board structures and roles
  • Corporate governance principles
  • Accountability and reporting frameworks

Module 11: Operational Management of SPVs

  • Project implementation and contract management
  • Stakeholder coordination (government, investors, regulators)
  • Managing contractors and service providers

Module 12: Monitoring, Evaluation, and Performance

  • Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
  • Performance monitoring systems
  • Reporting and compliance requirements

Day 5: Emerging Trends, Case Studies, and Practical Application

Module 13: PPPs in the Energy Sector

  • Independent Power Producers (IPPs)
  • Renewable energy PPPs (solar, wind, geothermal)
  • Grid modernization and transmission PPPs

Module 14: ESG, Sustainability, and Regulatory Compliance

  • Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) considerations
  • Safeguards and sustainability frameworks
  • Climate finance and green investments

Module 15: Case Studies and Practical Exercises

  • Regional and global PPP/SPV case studies
  • Group work: Designing an SPV for a power project
  • Simulation of PPP negotiation and structuring

TRAINING METHODOLOGY

  • Interactive lectures and expert facilitation
  • Case studies (energy sector focus)
  • Group discussions and peer learning
  • Practical exercises and simulations
  • Real-world project analysis

EXPECTED OUTCOME

Participants will leave with:

  • Practical skills to structure and manage SPVs
  • Improved capacity to engage investors and partners
  • Enhanced ability to deliver PPP projects effectively
  • Tools to ensure financial and operational sustainability

This training can also be customized for your institution upon request. You can also have it delivered at your preferred location (In-House, Classroom in Nairobi/Arusha/Mombasa/Naivasha/Kigali/Dubai/Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), or Online).

DIGITAL CERTIFICATION

Participants who successfully complete the programme will receive an official ECAS Institute Certificate of Completion recognized across public and private sector institutions.

introduction-to-climate-change-mitigatio.location: Nairobi - Kenya / Mombasa / Arusha / Kigali / Online
introduction-to-climate-change-mitigatio.summary: This flagship executive course on Introduction to Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Technology Responses equips climate change negotiators, government policymakers, humanitarian leaders, and adaptation specialists with comprehensive knowledge of UNFCCC Paris Agreement workstreams, NDC implementation, vulnerability analysis, and locally led climate action.
introduction-to-climate-change-mitigatio.content:
OVERVIEW

The Introduction to Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Technology Responses executive programme provides an authoritative, practitioner-driven exploration of international and national climate change policy, adaptation planning, and resilience building. As climate extremes intensify across Africa, governments, civil society, and development agencies must translate global Paris Agreement commitments into funded, gender-responsive, and locally led adaptation and mitigation actions.

Participants engage in hands-on policy simulations covering Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), Long-Term Low-Emission Development Strategies (LT-LEDS), Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) reporting, Loss and Damage mechanisms, and Climate Vulnerability and Capacity Analysis (CVCA).

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Climate Change Directors, UNFCCC National Focal Points, and Diplomatic Negotiators
  • National and Sub-National Development Planners, Policy Analysts, and Sectoral Ministry Leads
  • Humanitarian Aid Directors, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) Managers, and Resilience Specialists
  • Civil Society Advocates, Gender & Climate Justice Leads, and Climate Information Service Providers

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Master the scientific, policy, and operational dimensions of Introduction to Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Technology Responses.
  • Navigate UNFCCC party-driven processes, Global Stocktake outcomes, and international climate negotiations.
  • Mainstream climate change adaptation and NDC targets into national and county development plans.
  • Conduct Climate Vulnerability and Capacity Analysis (CVCA) and design Anticipatory Action protocols.
  • Operationalize Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF), MEL for adaptation, and Loss & Damage finance.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: Climate Science, Policy Architecture & Foundations of Introduction to Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Technology Responses

  • Observed and projected climate variability, attribution science, and sector-specific impacts in Africa
  • UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol, Paris Agreement architecture, and Global Stocktake (GST) mandates
  • National climate change acts, institutional governance arrangements, and multi-level coordination

Module 2: NDCs, LT-LEDS & Mainstreaming Adaptation into Development Planning

  • Formulating, costing, and updating Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0) and LT-LEDS
  • Integrating National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) into sectoral budgets and sub-national development plans
  • Technology Needs Assessments (TNAs), UNFCCC Technology Mechanism, and endogenous innovation

Module 3: Vulnerability Assessment, Early Warning & Anticipatory Action

  • Participatory Climate Vulnerability and Capacity Analysis (CVCA) and climate risk mapping
  • Climate Information Services (CIS), multi-hazard early warning systems, and forecast-based financing
  • Climate-induced human mobility, migration governance, human rights, and gender-responsive climate justice

Module 4: Transparency (ETF), Loss & Damage, and International Negotiations

  • Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF), Biennial Transparency Reports (BTRs), and national GHG inventories
  • Warsaw International Mechanism, Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, and disaster risk insurance
  • Negotiation diplomacy, coalition building (AGN, G77+China), and drafting UNFCCC decision text

Module 5: MEL for Adaptation, GCF Project Design & Capstone Simulation

  • Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) indicators for tracking adaptation and resilience outcomes
  • Structuring climate rationale and theory of change for Green Climate Fund (GCF) proposals
  • Capstone simulation: Policy briefing / NDC implementation action plan for your institution

climate-change-and-infrastructure-risks-.summary: This executive training programme on Climate Change and Infrastructure Risks, Vulnerability Assessment and Management equips energy planners, transport engineers, infrastructure developers, and policy regulators with practical frameworks for renewable energy deployment, e-mobility transition, and climate-resilient infrastructure engineering.
climate-change-and-infrastructure-risks-.content:
OVERVIEW

The Climate Change and Infrastructure Risks, Vulnerability Assessment and Management course is designed for senior professionals leading Africa's transition toward clean energy systems, low-carbon transport networks, and climate-resilient public infrastructure. Rapid urbanization and industrialization demand modern grid integration, electric mobility ecosystems, and infrastructure assets engineered to withstand extreme climate hazards.

Participants will examine renewable energy project finance (PPAs, mini-grids, battery storage), electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure and public transit decarbonization, and climate-proofing engineering standards for roads, energy, water, and urban assets.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Energy Regulatory Commissioners, Utility Managers, and Independent Power Producers (IPPs)

just-transition-policy-and-practice.content:
OVERVIEW

The Just Transition Policy and Practice masterclass is tailored for senior decision-makers navigating institutional transformation, regulatory complexity, and heightened public accountability. High-performing public agencies, state corporations, and private enterprises require visionary boards, agile strategic planning, robust anti-corruption safeguards, and citizen-centric policy design.

Drawing on global corporate governance codes (King IV, Mwongozo, OECD Guidelines), Balanced Scorecard execution, design thinking in policy reform, and diplomatic negotiation techniques, this programme equips leaders to drive lasting organizational excellence.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Board Chairpersons, Non-Executive Directors, Chief Executive Officers, and Managing Directors
  • Permanent/Principal Secretaries, County Executives, Directors-General, and Commissioners
  • Heads of Strategy, Corporate Planning, Risk, Legal, Compliance, and Internal Audit
  • Senior Diplomats, Policy Analysts, and Public Sector Reform Programme Leaders

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Demonstrate high-impact executive competence in Just Transition Policy and Practice.
  • Strengthen board oversight, fiduciary accountability, ethical culture, and enterprise risk governance.
  • Formulate and execute agile strategic plans using the Balanced Scorecard and Results-Based Management (RBM).
  • Lead public sector policy reforms, anti-corruption and AML compliance, and institutional change management.
  • Master high-stakes negotiation, crisis contingency planning, diplomacy, and stakeholder consensus-building.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: Executive Leadership Doctrines & Governance Architecture in Just Transition Policy and Practice

  • Modern corporate and public sector governance codes (OECD, King IV, Mwongozo) and board fiduciary duties
  • Transformational, adaptive, and ethical leadership in complex multi-stakeholder environments
  • Aligning institutional mandate with national development visions and global sustainability goals

Module 2: Strategic Planning, Balanced Scorecard & Results-Based Management (RBM)

  • Environmental scanning, scenario planning, and agile strategy formulation
  • Cascading strategic objectives using the Balanced Scorecard (BSC) and performance contracting
  • Results-Based Management (RBM), public service delivery innovation, and citizen/client value creation

Module 3: Enterprise Risk Oversight, Ethics, Anti-Corruption & Financial Integrity

  • Board-level Enterprise Risk Management (ERM), internal controls, and supervision of public enterprises
  • Anti-corruption reforms, Anti-Money Laundering (AML), asset declaration, and whistle-blower protection
  • Integrating Gender Equality, Diversity, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) into governance and leadership

Module 4: Policy Design, Diplomatic Negotiation & Crisis Leadership

  • Evidence-based sectoral policy analysis, design thinking, and regulatory impact assessment (RIA)
  • Principled negotiation, collective bargaining, alternative dispute resolution (ADR), and state protocol
  • Crisis management command structures, business continuity, and strategic contingency planning

Module 5: Leading Organizational Change & Executive Action Charter

  • Overcoming institutional resistance and embedding high-performance organizational culture
  • Case studies of successful public enterprise turnarounds and governance reforms in Africa
  • Executive clinic: Drafting a 90-Day Board/Institutional Transformation Charter

climate-finance-and-technology-mechanism.summary: This high-level executive programme on Climate Finance and Technology Mechanism equips public finance officers, central and commercial bankers, budget directors, and climate fund managers with advanced tools for climate-responsive budgeting, green bond structuring, climate risk modeling, and GCF/GEF resource mobilization.
climate-finance-and-technology-mechanism.content:
OVERVIEW

The Climate Finance and Technology Mechanism course bridges public financial management (PFM), commercial investment banking, and international climate finance architecture. Mobilizing and managing climate capital at scale requires rigorous fiscal tagging, bankable project preparation, robust fiduciary standards, and sophisticated climate financial risk analysis.

Participants gain practical experience in Climate Public Expenditure and Institutional Reviews (CPEIR), green budget coding, financial modeling for green projects, central bank climate stress testing, and fiduciary compliance for multilateral climate funds.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Budget Directors, Economists, and Accountants in Ministries of Finance, Treasury, and Planning
  • Central Bank Supervisors, Commercial Bank Risk Officers, and Sustainable Finance Heads
  • Internal & External Auditors, Forensic Accountants, and Parliamentary Fiscal Analysts
  • GCF/GEF National Designated Authorities (NDAs), Direct Access Entities, and Fund Managers

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Master analytical, budgetary, and investment tools essential for Climate Finance and Technology Mechanism.
  • Integrate climate change priorities into Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks (MTEF) and programme-based budgets.
  • Apply climate budget tagging, expenditure tracking, and green Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms.
  • Build financial models to appraise green projects, green/sustainability-linked bonds, and blended finance vehicles.
  • Strengthen internal audit, forensic fraud controls, and IFRS/IPSAS reporting for climate funds.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: International & Domestic Architecture of Climate Finance and Technology Mechanism

  • Global climate finance landscape: GCF, GEF, Adaptation Fund, Loss & Damage Fund, and MDBs
  • Green Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms and Climate Public Expenditure Reviews (CPEIR)
  • Aligning National Development Plans and NDC Investment Plans with sovereign fiscal strategy

Module 2: Climate-Responsive Budgeting, Tagging & Fiscal Tracking

  • Integrating climate criteria into budget circulars, MTEFs, and public investment management (PIMA)
  • Designing and operating Climate Budget Tagging (CBT) and IFMIS coding classifications
  • Green taxation, carbon fiscal instruments, fossil-fuel subsidy reform, and domestic revenue mobilization

Module 3: Green Project Appraisal, Financial Modelling & Capital Markets

  • Cost-benefit analysis, NPV/IRR sensitivity modeling, and shadow carbon pricing for green projects
  • Structuring green bonds, sukuk, sustainability-linked loans, and concessional blended finance
  • Developing bankable Concept Notes and Funding Proposals for GCF and bilateral donors

Module 4: Climate Financial Risk Analysis, Banking Supervision & Stress Testing

  • Physical and transition risk transmission channels across sovereigns, banks, and insurers
  • Scenario analysis (NGFS), portfolio climate stress testing, and Basel/central bank supervisory guidelines
  • Credit risk pricing, green asset ratios, and sustainable treasury management

Module 5: Fiduciary Standards, Climate Audit, Fraud Control & Reporting

  • IPSAS and IFRS S2 accounting standards for climate grants, concessional loans, and carbon assets
  • Risk-based internal auditing, forensic accounting, and procurement fraud prevention in green projects
  • Capstone simulation: Conducting a Climate Budget Tagging & Bankability Appraisal exercise

monitoring-evaluation-and-learning-mel-f.title: Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) for Climate Adaptation
monitoring-evaluation-and-learning-mel-f.location: Nairobi - Kenya / Mombasa / Arusha / Kigali / Online
monitoring-evaluation-and-learning-mel-f.summary: This practical executive course on Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) for Climate Adaptation equips project directors, procurement heads, PPP transaction advisors, and MEAL specialists with rigorous methodologies for project appraisal, public procurement compliance, contract management, donor resource mobilization, and results-based impact evaluation.
monitoring-evaluation-and-learning-mel-f.content:
OVERVIEW

The Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) for Climate Adaptation programme is designed to strengthen institutional delivery capacity across complex development programmes, public infrastructure investments, and donor-funded projects. Delays, cost overruns, procurement disputes, and weak monitoring frameworks often undermine project impact; this course provides proven tools to ensure value-for-money, fiduciary compliance, and measurable development outcomes.

Participants engage in practical simulations covering feasibility appraisal, World Bank/national public procurement procedures, Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) PPP structuring, winning grant proposal writing, and Outcome Harvesting / MEAL systems.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Project Directors, Programme Managers, and Project Management Office (PMO) Leads
  • Heads of Procurement, Supply Chain Managers, Tender Committee Members, and Contract Administrators
  • Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) Specialists and Impact Researchers
  • PPP Unit Officers, Infrastructure Transaction Advisors, and Grant/Resource Mobilization Managers

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Apply international standards and operational best practices in Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) for Climate Adaptation.
  • Conduct rigorous technical, economic, financial, and environmental feasibility appraisals.
  • Manage end-to-end public procurement, competitive bidding, tender evaluation, and FIDIC/NEC contract administration.
  • Structure bankable Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs), Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs), and donor grant proposals.
  • Design Results-Based MEAL frameworks, Theory of Change models, and impact evaluations.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: Strategic Planning, Governance & Legal Frameworks for Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) for Climate Adaptation

  • Project cycle management (PCM), Theory of Change (ToC), and Logical Framework Approach (LFA)
  • Public procurement statutes, World Bank/AfDB procurement regulations, and PPP legal frameworks
  • Stakeholder mapping, consortium governance, and institutional risk allocation matrices

Module 2: Feasibility Analysis, Appraisal & Resource Mobilization

  • Technical, financial, economic (ERR/NPV), and social/environmental appraisal of projects
  • Structuring Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs), concession agreements, and blended project finance
  • Donor intelligence, competitive grant proposal writing, and financial sustainability planning

Module 3: Procurement Planning, Tendering & Contract Management

  • Strategic procurement planning, drafting standard bidding documents (SBDs), and Terms of Reference (ToRs)
  • Bid evaluation methodologies, value-for-money analysis, and contract negotiation techniques
  • Contract administration, variation management, SLA monitoring, and dispute resolution

Module 4: Results-Based MEAL, Safeguards & Performance Contracting

  • Designing KPI indicator matrices, baseline surveys, and Outcome Harvesting methodologies
  • Social safeguards, involuntary resettlement action plans (RAP), and rights-based project delivery
  • Earned Value Management (EVM), project restructuring, and turnaround of stalled projects

Module 5: Audit Readiness, Impact Evaluation & Capstone Clinic

  • Counterfactual impact evaluation (RCTs, quasi-experimental designs) and value-for-money audits
  • Preventing procurement fraud, collusion, and audit queries in public and donor projects
  • Capstone workshop: Developing a complete Procurement Plan, PPP Term Sheet, or MEAL Framework

climate-and-disaster-risk-finance-and-in.title: Climate and Disaster Risk Finance and Insurance & Civil Society Engagement
climate-and-disaster-risk-finance-and-in.location: Nairobi - Kenya / Mombasa / Arusha / Kigali / Online
climate-and-disaster-risk-finance-and-in.summary: This high-level executive programme on Climate and Disaster Risk Finance and Insurance & Civil Society Engagement equips public finance officers, central and commercial bankers, budget directors, and climate fund managers with advanced tools for climate-responsive budgeting, green bond structuring, climate risk modeling, and GCF/GEF resource mobilization.
climate-and-disaster-risk-finance-and-in.content:
OVERVIEW

The Climate and Disaster Risk Finance and Insurance & Civil Society Engagement course bridges public financial management (PFM), commercial investment banking, and international climate finance architecture. Mobilizing and managing climate capital at scale requires rigorous fiscal tagging, bankable project preparation, robust fiduciary standards, and sophisticated climate financial risk analysis.

Participants gain practical experience in Climate Public Expenditure and Institutional Reviews (CPEIR), green budget coding, financial modeling for green projects, central bank climate stress testing, and fiduciary compliance for multilateral climate funds.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Budget Directors, Economists, and Accountants in Ministries of Finance, Treasury, and Planning
  • Central Bank Supervisors, Commercial Bank Risk Officers, and Sustainable Finance Heads
  • Internal & External Auditors, Forensic Accountants, and Parliamentary Fiscal Analysts
  • GCF/GEF National Designated Authorities (NDAs), Direct Access Entities, and Fund Managers

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Master analytical, budgetary, and investment tools essential for Climate and Disaster Risk Finance and Insurance & Civil Society Engagement.
  • Integrate climate change priorities into Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks (MTEF) and programme-based budgets.
  • Apply climate budget tagging, expenditure tracking, and green Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms.
  • Build financial models to appraise green projects, green/sustainability-linked bonds, and blended finance vehicles.
  • Strengthen internal audit, forensic fraud controls, and IFRS/IPSAS reporting for climate funds.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: International & Domestic Architecture of Climate and Disaster Risk Finance and Insurance & Civil Society Engagement

  • Global climate finance landscape: GCF, GEF, Adaptation Fund, Loss & Damage Fund, and MDBs
  • Green Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms and Climate Public Expenditure Reviews (CPEIR)
  • Aligning National Development Plans and NDC Investment Plans with sovereign fiscal strategy

Module 2: Climate-Responsive Budgeting, Tagging & Fiscal Tracking

  • Integrating climate criteria into budget circulars, MTEFs, and public investment management (PIMA)
  • Designing and operating Climate Budget Tagging (CBT) and IFMIS coding classifications
  • Green taxation, carbon fiscal instruments, fossil-fuel subsidy reform, and domestic revenue mobilization

Module 3: Green Project Appraisal, Financial Modelling & Capital Markets

  • Cost-benefit analysis, NPV/IRR sensitivity modeling, and shadow carbon pricing for green projects
  • Structuring green bonds, sukuk, sustainability-linked loans, and concessional blended finance
  • Developing bankable Concept Notes and Funding Proposals for GCF and bilateral donors

Module 4: Climate Financial Risk Analysis, Banking Supervision & Stress Testing

  • Physical and transition risk transmission channels across sovereigns, banks, and insurers
  • Scenario analysis (NGFS), portfolio climate stress testing, and Basel/central bank supervisory guidelines
  • Credit risk pricing, green asset ratios, and sustainable treasury management

Module 5: Fiduciary Standards, Climate Audit, Fraud Control & Reporting

  • IPSAS and IFRS S2 accounting standards for climate grants, concessional loans, and carbon assets
  • Risk-based internal auditing, forensic accounting, and procurement fraud prevention in green projects
  • Capstone simulation: Conducting a Climate Budget Tagging & Bankability Appraisal exercise

Participants engage in hands-on policy simulations covering Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), Long-Term Low-Emission Development Strategies (LT-LEDS), Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) reporting, Loss and Damage mechanisms, and Climate Vulnerability and Capacity Analysis (CVCA).

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Climate Change Directors, UNFCCC National Focal Points, and Diplomatic Negotiators
  • National and Sub-National Development Planners, Policy Analysts, and Sectoral Ministry Leads
  • Humanitarian Aid Directors, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) Managers, and Resilience Specialists
  • Civil Society Advocates, Gender & Climate Justice Leads, and Climate Information Service Providers

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Master the scientific, policy, and operational dimensions of Understanding the Climate Crisis.
  • Navigate UNFCCC party-driven processes, Global Stocktake outcomes, and international climate negotiations.
  • Mainstream climate change adaptation and NDC targets into national and county development plans.
  • Conduct Climate Vulnerability and Capacity Analysis (CVCA) and design Anticipatory Action protocols.
  • Operationalize Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF), MEL for adaptation, and Loss & Damage finance.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: Climate Science, Policy Architecture & Foundations of Understanding the Climate Crisis

  • Observed and projected climate variability, attribution science, and sector-specific impacts in Africa
  • UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol, Paris Agreement architecture, and Global Stocktake (GST) mandates
  • National climate change acts, institutional governance arrangements, and multi-level coordination

Module 2: NDCs, LT-LEDS & Mainstreaming Adaptation into Development Planning

  • Formulating, costing, and updating Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0) and LT-LEDS
  • Integrating National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) into sectoral budgets and sub-national development plans
  • Technology Needs Assessments (TNAs), UNFCCC Technology Mechanism, and endogenous innovation

Module 3: Vulnerability Assessment, Early Warning & Anticipatory Action

  • Participatory Climate Vulnerability and Capacity Analysis (CVCA) and climate risk mapping
  • Climate Information Services (CIS), multi-hazard early warning systems, and forecast-based financing
  • Climate-induced human mobility, migration governance, human rights, and gender-responsive climate justice

Module 4: Transparency (ETF), Loss & Damage, and International Negotiations

  • Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF), Biennial Transparency Reports (BTRs), and national GHG inventories
  • Warsaw International Mechanism, Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, and disaster risk insurance
  • Negotiation diplomacy, coalition building (AGN, G77+China), and drafting UNFCCC decision text

Module 5: MEL for Adaptation, GCF Project Design & Capstone Simulation

  • Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) indicators for tracking adaptation and resilience outcomes
  • Structuring climate rationale and theory of change for Green Climate Fund (GCF) proposals
  • Capstone simulation: Policy briefing / NDC implementation action plan for your institution

introduction-to-ecosystem-based-adaptati.title: Introduction to Ecosystem-Based Adaptation (EbA)
introduction-to-ecosystem-based-adaptati.location: Nairobi - Kenya / Mombasa / Arusha / Kigali / Online
introduction-to-ecosystem-based-adaptati.summary: This specialized executive course on Introduction to Ecosystem-Based Adaptation (EbA) provides environmental planners, forestry and water resource managers, and conservation practitioners with practical tools for ecosystem restoration, watershed governance, and nature-based climate resilience. Participants master spatial planning, hydrological risk assessment, and sustainable natural resource financing.
introduction-to-ecosystem-based-adaptati.content:
OVERVIEW

The Introduction to Ecosystem-Based Adaptation (EbA) programme equips senior practitioners and policymakers with science-based methodologies to sustainably manage forests, river basins, wetlands, and critical ecological landscapes. Healthy watersheds and forest ecosystems underpin water security, disaster risk reduction, and rural livelihoods across Africa.

Combining hydrological and ecological modeling, IUCN Global Standards for Nature-Based Solutions (NbS), and participatory catchment governance, this course enables participants to design bankable landscape restoration initiatives and integrated water-forestry policies.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Forestry Conservators, Catchment Managers, and Water Resource Authority Officials
  • Environmental Planners, Hydrologists, and Ecosystem Restoration Specialists
  • Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Adaptation Leads in Government and NGOs
  • Natural Resource Economists and Conservation Project Developers

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Apply international best practices and technical standards in Introduction to Ecosystem-Based Adaptation (EbA).
  • Conduct watershed vulnerability assessments, forest inventory mapping, and ecosystem service valuation.
  • Design Nature-Based Solutions (NbS) and Ecosystem-Based Adaptation (EbA) interventions for flood and drought resilience.
  • Establish multi-stakeholder catchment governance and community forest management agreements.
  • Mobilize climate, biodiversity, and REDD+ finance for landscape-scale conservation programmes.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: Ecological Principles & Governance Frameworks in Introduction to Ecosystem-Based Adaptation (EbA)

  • Forest-water-climate nexus and ecosystem services in tropical and dryland landscapes
  • National water and forestry legislation, transboundary basin agreements, and IUCN NbS standards
  • Baseline ecological assessment and Degradation / Deforestation driver analysis

Module 2: Hydrological Assessment, Catchment Planning & Forest Management

  • Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) and river basin allocation modeling
  • Sustainable silviculture, afforestation/reforestation (ARR), and REDD+ technical design
  • GIS and remote sensing tools for forest cover, land-use change, and hydrological monitoring

Module 3: Nature-Based Solutions (NbS) for Disaster & Climate Resilience

  • Designing green-grey infrastructure for flood attenuation, slope stabilization, and drought buffering
  • Riparian buffer restoration, wetland conservation, and groundwater recharge strategies
  • Community-based natural resource management (CBNRM) and indigenous knowledge integration

Module 4: Natural Capital Valuation & Conservation Financing Mechanisms

  • Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES), water funds, and biodiversity offsets
  • Accessing Green Climate Fund (GCF), GEF, and high-integrity forestry carbon markets
  • Private sector partnerships and sustainable timber/non-timber forest product value chains

Module 5: Ecological Monitoring, MRV & Capstone Landscape Action Plan

  • Biophysical and socio-economic indicators for tracking ecosystem restoration impact
  • Field-based case studies from major African water towers and river basins
  • Action planning workshop: Structuring a landscape or catchment intervention roadmap

This training can also be customized for your institution upon request. You can also have it delivered at your preferred location (In-House, Classroom in Nairobi/Arusha/Mombasa/Naivasha/Kigali/Dubai/Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), or Online).

TRAINING FEE

  • Kenyans (5 days): USD 1,200
  • Kenyans (10 working days / 2 Weeks): USD 2,000
  • International participants (10 working days / 2 Weeks): USD 2,500
  • 3–4 Weeks Executive Programme: USD 3,000
  • The course fee covers the course tuition, training materials, stationery, and daytime refreshments during physical sessions.
  • We are open for institutional negotiations and can customize courses based on your availability, cohort size, and budget.

climate-risk-modelling-and-scenario-anal.title: Climate Risk Modelling and Scenario Analysis for Sustainable Development
climate-risk-modelling-and-scenario-anal.location: Nairobi - Kenya / Mombasa / Arusha / Kigali / Online
climate-risk-modelling-and-scenario-anal.summary: This high-level executive programme on Climate Risk Modelling and Scenario Analysis for Sustainable Development equips public finance officers, central and commercial bankers, budget directors, and climate fund managers with advanced tools for climate-responsive budgeting, green bond structuring, climate risk modeling, and GCF/GEF resource mobilization.
climate-risk-modelling-and-scenario-anal.content:
OVERVIEW

The Climate Risk Modelling and Scenario Analysis for Sustainable Development course bridges public financial management (PFM), commercial investment banking, and international climate finance architecture. Mobilizing and managing climate capital at scale requires rigorous fiscal tagging, bankable project preparation, robust fiduciary standards, and sophisticated climate financial risk analysis.

Participants gain practical experience in Climate Public Expenditure and Institutional Reviews (CPEIR), green budget coding, financial modeling for green projects, central bank climate stress testing, and fiduciary compliance for multilateral climate funds.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Budget Directors, Economists, and Accountants in Ministries of Finance, Treasury, and Planning
  • Central Bank Supervisors, Commercial Bank Risk Officers, and Sustainable Finance Heads
  • Internal & External Auditors, Forensic Accountants, and Parliamentary Fiscal Analysts
  • GCF/GEF National Designated Authorities (NDAs), Direct Access Entities, and Fund Managers

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Master analytical, budgetary, and investment tools essential for Climate Risk Modelling and Scenario Analysis for Sustainable Development.
  • Integrate climate change priorities into Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks (MTEF) and programme-based budgets.
  • Apply climate budget tagging, expenditure tracking, and green Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms.
  • Build financial models to appraise green projects, green/sustainability-linked bonds, and blended finance vehicles.
  • Strengthen internal audit, forensic fraud controls, and IFRS/IPSAS reporting for climate funds.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: International & Domestic Architecture of Climate Risk Modelling and Scenario Analysis for Sustainable Development

  • Global climate finance landscape: GCF, GEF, Adaptation Fund, Loss & Damage Fund, and MDBs
  • Green Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms and Climate Public Expenditure Reviews (CPEIR)
  • Aligning National Development Plans and NDC Investment Plans with sovereign fiscal strategy

Module 2: Climate-Responsive Budgeting, Tagging & Fiscal Tracking

  • Integrating climate criteria into budget circulars, MTEFs, and public investment management (PIMA)
  • Designing and operating Climate Budget Tagging (CBT) and IFMIS coding classifications
  • Green taxation, carbon fiscal instruments, fossil-fuel subsidy reform, and domestic revenue mobilization

Module 3: Green Project Appraisal, Financial Modelling & Capital Markets

  • Cost-benefit analysis, NPV/IRR sensitivity modeling, and shadow carbon pricing for green projects
  • Structuring green bonds, sukuk, sustainability-linked loans, and concessional blended finance
  • Developing bankable Concept Notes and Funding Proposals for GCF and bilateral donors

Module 4: Climate Financial Risk Analysis, Banking Supervision & Stress Testing

  • Physical and transition risk transmission channels across sovereigns, banks, and insurers
  • Scenario analysis (NGFS), portfolio climate stress testing, and Basel/central bank supervisory guidelines
  • Credit risk pricing, green asset ratios, and sustainable treasury management

Module 5: Fiduciary Standards, Climate Audit, Fraud Control & Reporting

  • IPSAS and IFRS S2 accounting standards for climate grants, concessional loans, and carbon assets
  • Risk-based internal auditing, forensic accounting, and procurement fraud prevention in green projects
  • Capstone simulation: Conducting a Climate Budget Tagging & Bankability Appraisal exercise

carbon-markets.content:
OVERVIEW

Practical executive courses on carbon accounting, MRV, emissions trading, agricultural carbon credit markets, nature-based solutions, and corporate ESG reporting & disclosure.

FEATURED EXECUTIVE COURSES (CLICK TO VIEW FULL CURRICULUM)

  • Carbon Accounting & Carbon Offsetting Course (5 Days)
  • Agricultural Carbon Credit Markets (5 Days)
  • Training on Carbon Markets and Trading (5 Days)
  • Certified Expert in Environmental Accounting, Leadership and Sustainability (5 Days)
  • Business Sustainability Management (5 Days)
  • Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Masterclass (5 Days)

2026 EXECUTIVE TRAINING CATALOGUE IN THIS CATEGORY

  • Carbon Markets and Emissions Trading
  • Carbon Accounting and MRV (Measurement, Reporting and Verification)
  • Carbon Credit Quality & Standards
  • Carbon Projects Design, Development, Verification and Reporting
  • Climate Financing & Nature-Based Solutions (NbS)
  • Carbon Trading, Finance & Risk Management
  • Introduction to ESG and Sustainable Finance
  • Environmental, Social and Governance Risks and Opportunities
  • Integrating ESG into Treasury Management
  • ESG Risk Assessment, Reporting and Disclosure

TRAINING CUSTOMIZATION

This training can also be customized for your institution upon request. You can also have it delivered at your preferred location (In-House, Classroom in Nairobi/Arusha/Mombasa/Naivasha/Kigali/Dubai/Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), or Online).

DIGITAL CERTIFICATION

Participants who successfully complete the programme will receive an official ECAS Institute Certificate of Completion recognized across public and private sector institutions.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Participants should be reasonably proficient in English. During the trainings, participants should come with their own laptops for practical sessions and simulations.

TRAINING FEE

  • Kenyans (5 days): USD 1,200
  • Kenyans (10 working days / 2 Weeks): USD 2,000
  • International participants (10 working days / 2 Weeks): USD 2,500
  • 3–4 Weeks Executive Programme: USD 3,000
  • The course fee covers the course tuition, training materials, stationery, and daytime refreshments during physical sessions.
  • We are open for institutional negotiations and can customize courses based on your availability, cohort size, and budget.

carbon-markets-and-emissions-trading.summary: This practical executive course on Carbon Markets and Emissions Trading trains sustainability directors, carbon project developers, and ESG analysts in GHG accounting (ISO 14064 / GHG Protocol), Paris Agreement Article 6 mechanisms, Voluntary Carbon Markets (VCM), and international ESG reporting standards (ISSB IFRS S1/S2, GRI, CSRD).
carbon-markets-and-emissions-trading.content:
OVERVIEW

The Carbon Markets and Emissions Trading executive programme delivers hands-on technical mastery of carbon market mechanics, greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory accounting, and corporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure. As sovereigns enact domestic carbon regulations and global investors mandate assured climate disclosures, organizations must build internal capacity to quantify emissions, originate high-integrity carbon credits, and report ESG performance accurately.

Participants work through real-world project design documents (PDDs), MRV digital platforms, Article 6.2/6.4 authorization workflows, Core Carbon Principles (ICVCM), and double-materiality ESG reporting templates.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Carbon Project Developers, Climate Change Directors, and National Article 6 Focal Points
  • Chief Sustainability Officers (CSOs), ESG Managers, and Corporate Responsibility Leads
  • Financial Controllers, Internal Auditors, and Investment Risk Analysts
  • Environmental Consultants, Verifiers (VVBs), and Legal/Regulatory Compliance Officers

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Execute end-to-end technical workflows in Carbon Markets and Emissions Trading aligned with global standards.
  • Quantify Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 GHG emissions using the GHG Protocol and ISO 14064-1.
  • Navigate Compliance (ETS, CBAM, Article 6 ITMOs) and Voluntary Carbon Markets (Verra VCS, Gold Standard).
  • Originate, validate, verify, and monetize high-integrity carbon credits while managing reversal and legal risks.
  • Prepare investor-grade sustainability and ESG disclosures aligned with ISSB (IFRS S1 & S2), GRI, and TCFD.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: Global Architecture & Regulatory Frameworks for Carbon Markets and Emissions Trading

  • Paris Agreement Article 6 (6.2 Cooperative Approaches & 6.4 Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism)
  • Voluntary Carbon Market (VCM) integrity standards: ICVCM Core Carbon Principles & VCMI Claims Code
  • National carbon market regulations, community benefit-sharing legislation, and CBAM implications

Module 2: Corporate GHG Accounting, Baseline Setting & Net-Zero Pathways

  • GHG Protocol Corporate Standard & ISO 14064: Quantifying Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 value-chain emissions
  • Setting Science-Based Targets (SBTi), marginal abatement cost curves (MACC), and internal carbon pricing
  • Designing robust Measurement, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) and digital MRV (dMRV) systems

Module 3: Carbon Project Origination, Methodologies & Verification

  • Project cycle from Feasibility & PIN to Project Design Document (PDD), Validation, and Verification
  • Additionality testing, baseline scenarios, leakage assessment, and permanence/buffer pool management
  • Sectoral methodologies: REDD+/ARR forestry, clean cooking, renewable energy, e-mobility, and soil carbon

Module 4: ESG Strategy, Materiality Assessment & Mandatory Disclosures

  • Conducting double-materiality assessments and integrating ESG into enterprise risk management (ERM)
  • Reporting with IFRS S1 & S2 (ISSB), Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), TCFD, and EU CSRD frameworks
  • Preventing greenwashing, preparing for third-party ESG assurance, and improving ESG ratings

Module 5: Carbon Pricing, Offtake Contracting & Capstone Simulation

  • Structuring Emissions Reduction Purchase Agreements (ERPAs), spot/forward pricing, and registry operations
  • Managing tax, accounting, and sovereign Corresponding Adjustment (CA) requirements
  • Hands-on clinic: Drafting a Carbon Project Concept Note or Corporate ESG Disclosure Report

climate-financing-nature-based-solutions.title: Climate Financing & Nature-Based Solutions (NbS)
climate-financing-nature-based-solutions.location: Nairobi - Kenya / Mombasa / Arusha / Kigali / Online
climate-financing-nature-based-solutions.summary: This specialized executive course on Climate Financing & Nature-Based Solutions (NbS) provides environmental planners, forestry and water resource managers, and conservation practitioners with practical tools for ecosystem restoration, watershed governance, and nature-based climate resilience. Participants master spatial planning, hydrological risk assessment, and sustainable natural resource financing.
climate-financing-nature-based-solutions.content:
OVERVIEW

The Climate Financing & Nature-Based Solutions (NbS) programme equips senior practitioners and policymakers with science-based methodologies to sustainably manage forests, river basins, wetlands, and critical ecological landscapes. Healthy watersheds and forest ecosystems underpin water security, disaster risk reduction, and rural livelihoods across Africa.

Combining hydrological and ecological modeling, IUCN Global Standards for Nature-Based Solutions (NbS), and participatory catchment governance, this course enables participants to design bankable landscape restoration initiatives and integrated water-forestry policies.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Forestry Conservators, Catchment Managers, and Water Resource Authority Officials
  • Environmental Planners, Hydrologists, and Ecosystem Restoration Specialists
  • Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Adaptation Leads in Government and NGOs
  • Natural Resource Economists and Conservation Project Developers

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Apply international best practices and technical standards in Climate Financing & Nature-Based Solutions (NbS).
  • Conduct watershed vulnerability assessments, forest inventory mapping, and ecosystem service valuation.
  • Design Nature-Based Solutions (NbS) and Ecosystem-Based Adaptation (EbA) interventions for flood and drought resilience.
  • Establish multi-stakeholder catchment governance and community forest management agreements.
  • Mobilize climate, biodiversity, and REDD+ finance for landscape-scale conservation programmes.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: Ecological Principles & Governance Frameworks in Climate Financing & Nature-Based Solutions (NbS)

  • Forest-water-climate nexus and ecosystem services in tropical and dryland landscapes
  • National water and forestry legislation, transboundary basin agreements, and IUCN NbS standards
  • Baseline ecological assessment and Degradation / Deforestation driver analysis

Module 2: Hydrological Assessment, Catchment Planning & Forest Management

  • Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) and river basin allocation modeling
  • Sustainable silviculture, afforestation/reforestation (ARR), and REDD+ technical design
  • GIS and remote sensing tools for forest cover, land-use change, and hydrological monitoring

Module 3: Nature-Based Solutions (NbS) for Disaster & Climate Resilience

  • Designing green-grey infrastructure for flood attenuation, slope stabilization, and drought buffering
  • Riparian buffer restoration, wetland conservation, and groundwater recharge strategies
  • Community-based natural resource management (CBNRM) and indigenous knowledge integration

Module 4: Natural Capital Valuation & Conservation Financing Mechanisms

  • Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES), water funds, and biodiversity offsets
  • Accessing Green Climate Fund (GCF), GEF, and high-integrity forestry carbon markets
  • Private sector partnerships and sustainable timber/non-timber forest product value chains

Module 5: Ecological Monitoring, MRV & Capstone Landscape Action Plan

  • Biophysical and socio-economic indicators for tracking ecosystem restoration impact
  • Field-based case studies from major African water towers and river basins
  • Action planning workshop: Structuring a landscape or catchment intervention roadmap

integrating-esg-into-treasury-management.summary: This practical executive course on Integrating ESG into Treasury Management trains sustainability directors, carbon project developers, and ESG analysts in GHG accounting (ISO 14064 / GHG Protocol), Paris Agreement Article 6 mechanisms, Voluntary Carbon Markets (VCM), and international ESG reporting standards (ISSB IFRS S1/S2, GRI, CSRD).
integrating-esg-into-treasury-management.content:
OVERVIEW

The Integrating ESG into Treasury Management executive programme delivers hands-on technical mastery of carbon market mechanics, greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory accounting, and corporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure. As sovereigns enact domestic carbon regulations and global investors mandate assured climate disclosures, organizations must build internal capacity to quantify emissions, originate high-integrity carbon credits, and report ESG performance accurately.

Participants work through real-world project design documents (PDDs), MRV digital platforms, Article 6.2/6.4 authorization workflows, Core Carbon Principles (ICVCM), and double-materiality ESG reporting templates.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Carbon Project Developers, Climate Change Directors, and National Article 6 Focal Points
  • Chief Sustainability Officers (CSOs), ESG Managers, and Corporate Responsibility Leads
  • Financial Controllers, Internal Auditors, and Investment Risk Analysts
  • Environmental Consultants, Verifiers (VVBs), and Legal/Regulatory Compliance Officers

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Execute end-to-end technical workflows in Integrating ESG into Treasury Management aligned with global standards.
  • Quantify Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 GHG emissions using the GHG Protocol and ISO 14064-1.
  • Navigate Compliance (ETS, CBAM, Article 6 ITMOs) and Voluntary Carbon Markets (Verra VCS, Gold Standard).
  • Originate, validate, verify, and monetize high-integrity carbon credits while managing reversal and legal risks.
  • Prepare investor-grade sustainability and ESG disclosures aligned with ISSB (IFRS S1 & S2), GRI, and TCFD.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: Global Architecture & Regulatory Frameworks for Integrating ESG into Treasury Management

  • Paris Agreement Article 6 (6.2 Cooperative Approaches & 6.4 Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism)
  • Voluntary Carbon Market (VCM) integrity standards: ICVCM Core Carbon Principles & VCMI Claims Code
  • National carbon market regulations, community benefit-sharing legislation, and CBAM implications

Module 2: Corporate GHG Accounting, Baseline Setting & Net-Zero Pathways

  • GHG Protocol Corporate Standard & ISO 14064: Quantifying Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 value-chain emissions
  • Setting Science-Based Targets (SBTi), marginal abatement cost curves (MACC), and internal carbon pricing
  • Designing robust Measurement, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) and digital MRV (dMRV) systems

Module 3: Carbon Project Origination, Methodologies & Verification

  • Project cycle from Feasibility & PIN to Project Design Document (PDD), Validation, and Verification
  • Additionality testing, baseline scenarios, leakage assessment, and permanence/buffer pool management
  • Sectoral methodologies: REDD+/ARR forestry, clean cooking, renewable energy, e-mobility, and soil carbon

Module 4: ESG Strategy, Materiality Assessment & Mandatory Disclosures

  • Conducting double-materiality assessments and integrating ESG into enterprise risk management (ERM)
  • Reporting with IFRS S1 & S2 (ISSB), Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), TCFD, and EU CSRD frameworks
  • Preventing greenwashing, preparing for third-party ESG assurance, and improving ESG ratings

Module 5: Carbon Pricing, Offtake Contracting & Capstone Simulation

agile-business-strategy-for-organisation.summary: This senior executive programme on Agile Business Strategy for Organisational Development and Sustainability empowers board directors, permanent secretaries, chief executives, and public policy leaders with transformative frameworks for corporate governance, ethical leadership, public sector innovation, strategic planning, and results-based institutional reform.
agile-business-strategy-for-organisation.content:
OVERVIEW

The Agile Business Strategy for Organisational Development and Sustainability masterclass is tailored for senior decision-makers navigating institutional transformation, regulatory complexity, and heightened public accountability. High-performing public agencies, state corporations, and private enterprises require visionary boards, agile strategic planning, robust anti-corruption safeguards, and citizen-centric policy design.

Drawing on global corporate governance codes (King IV, Mwongozo, OECD Guidelines), Balanced Scorecard execution, design thinking in policy reform, and diplomatic negotiation techniques, this programme equips leaders to drive lasting organizational excellence.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Board Chairpersons, Non-Executive Directors, Chief Executive Officers, and Managing Directors
  • Permanent/Principal Secretaries, County Executives, Directors-General, and Commissioners
  • Heads of Strategy, Corporate Planning, Risk, Legal, Compliance, and Internal Audit
  • Senior Diplomats, Policy Analysts, and Public Sector Reform Programme Leaders

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Demonstrate high-impact executive competence in Agile Business Strategy for Organisational Development and Sustainability.
  • Strengthen board oversight, fiduciary accountability, ethical culture, and enterprise risk governance.
  • Formulate and execute agile strategic plans using the Balanced Scorecard and Results-Based Management (RBM).
  • Lead public sector policy reforms, anti-corruption and AML compliance, and institutional change management.
  • Master high-stakes negotiation, crisis contingency planning, diplomacy, and stakeholder consensus-building.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: Executive Leadership Doctrines & Governance Architecture in Agile Business Strategy for Organisational Development and Sustainability

  • Modern corporate and public sector governance codes (OECD, King IV, Mwongozo) and board fiduciary duties
  • Transformational, adaptive, and ethical leadership in complex multi-stakeholder environments
  • Aligning institutional mandate with national development visions and global sustainability goals

Module 2: Strategic Planning, Balanced Scorecard & Results-Based Management (RBM)

  • Environmental scanning, scenario planning, and agile strategy formulation
  • Cascading strategic objectives using the Balanced Scorecard (BSC) and performance contracting
  • Results-Based Management (RBM), public service delivery innovation, and citizen/client value creation

Module 3: Enterprise Risk Oversight, Ethics, Anti-Corruption & Financial Integrity

  • Board-level Enterprise Risk Management (ERM), internal controls, and supervision of public enterprises
  • Anti-corruption reforms, Anti-Money Laundering (AML), asset declaration, and whistle-blower protection
  • Integrating Gender Equality, Diversity, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) into governance and leadership

Module 4: Policy Design, Diplomatic Negotiation & Crisis Leadership

  • Evidence-based sectoral policy analysis, design thinking, and regulatory impact assessment (RIA)
  • Principled negotiation, collective bargaining, alternative dispute resolution (ADR), and state protocol
  • Crisis management command structures, business continuity, and strategic contingency planning

Module 5: Leading Organizational Change & Executive Action Charter

  • Overcoming institutional resistance and embedding high-performance organizational culture
  • Case studies of successful public enterprise turnarounds and governance reforms in Africa
  • Executive clinic: Drafting a 90-Day Board/Institutional Transformation Charter

anti-corruption-and-fraud-prevention-ant.title: Anti-Corruption and Fraud Prevention, Anti-Money Laundering and Financial Crime
anti-corruption-and-fraud-prevention-ant.location: Nairobi - Kenya / Mombasa / Arusha / Kigali / Online
anti-corruption-and-fraud-prevention-ant.summary: This high-level executive programme on Anti-Corruption and Fraud Prevention, Anti-Money Laundering and Financial Crime equips public finance officers, central and commercial bankers, budget directors, and climate fund managers with advanced tools for climate-responsive budgeting, green bond structuring, climate risk modeling, and GCF/GEF resource mobilization.
anti-corruption-and-fraud-prevention-ant.content:
OVERVIEW

The Anti-Corruption and Fraud Prevention, Anti-Money Laundering and Financial Crime course bridges public financial management (PFM), commercial investment banking, and international climate finance architecture. Mobilizing and managing climate capital at scale requires rigorous fiscal tagging, bankable project preparation, robust fiduciary standards, and sophisticated climate financial risk analysis.

Participants gain practical experience in Climate Public Expenditure and Institutional Reviews (CPEIR), green budget coding, financial modeling for green projects, central bank climate stress testing, and fiduciary compliance for multilateral climate funds.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Budget Directors, Economists, and Accountants in Ministries of Finance, Treasury, and Planning
  • Central Bank Supervisors, Commercial Bank Risk Officers, and Sustainable Finance Heads
  • Internal & External Auditors, Forensic Accountants, and Parliamentary Fiscal Analysts
  • GCF/GEF National Designated Authorities (NDAs), Direct Access Entities, and Fund Managers

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Master analytical, budgetary, and investment tools essential for Anti-Corruption and Fraud Prevention, Anti-Money Laundering and Financial Crime.
  • Integrate climate change priorities into Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks (MTEF) and programme-based budgets.
  • Apply climate budget tagging, expenditure tracking, and green Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms.
  • Build financial models to appraise green projects, green/sustainability-linked bonds, and blended finance vehicles.
  • Strengthen internal audit, forensic fraud controls, and IFRS/IPSAS reporting for climate funds.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: International & Domestic Architecture of Anti-Corruption and Fraud Prevention, Anti-Money Laundering and Financial Crime

  • Global climate finance landscape: GCF, GEF, Adaptation Fund, Loss & Damage Fund, and MDBs
  • Green Public Financial Management (PFM) reforms and Climate Public Expenditure Reviews (CPEIR)
  • Aligning National Development Plans and NDC Investment Plans with sovereign fiscal strategy

Module 2: Climate-Responsive Budgeting, Tagging & Fiscal Tracking

  • Integrating climate criteria into budget circulars, MTEFs, and public investment management (PIMA)
  • Designing and operating Climate Budget Tagging (CBT) and IFMIS coding classifications
  • Green taxation, carbon fiscal instruments, fossil-fuel subsidy reform, and domestic revenue mobilization

Module 3: Green Project Appraisal, Financial Modelling & Capital Markets

  • Cost-benefit analysis, NPV/IRR sensitivity modeling, and shadow carbon pricing for green projects
  • Structuring green bonds, sukuk, sustainability-linked loans, and concessional blended finance
  • Developing bankable Concept Notes and Funding Proposals for GCF and bilateral donors

Module 4: Climate Financial Risk Analysis, Banking Supervision & Stress Testing

  • Physical and transition risk transmission channels across sovereigns, banks, and insurers
  • Scenario analysis (NGFS), portfolio climate stress testing, and Basel/central bank supervisory guidelines
  • Credit risk pricing, green asset ratios, and sustainable treasury management

Module 5: Fiduciary Standards, Climate Audit, Fraud Control & Reporting

  • IPSAS and IFRS S2 accounting standards for climate grants, concessional loans, and carbon assets
  • Risk-based internal auditing, forensic accounting, and procurement fraud prevention in green projects
  • Capstone simulation: Conducting a Climate Budget Tagging & Bankability Appraisal exercise

conducting-environmental-impact-assessme.title: Conducting Environmental Impact Assessment for Projects and Operations
conducting-environmental-impact-assessme.location: Nairobi - Kenya / Mombasa / Arusha / Kigali / Online
conducting-environmental-impact-assessme.summary: This technical executive course on Conducting Environmental Impact Assessment for Projects and Operations equips environmental regulators, EHS managers, urban planners, and infrastructure safeguard specialists with practical methodologies for air quality monitoring, industrial emissions control, Environmental & Social Impact Assessments (ESIA), and ISO 14001/45001 compliance.
conducting-environmental-impact-assessme.content:
OVERVIEW

The Conducting Environmental Impact Assessment for Projects and Operations training programme provides rigorous, practitioner-focused instruction on environmental protection, occupational health and safety (HSE), urban air quality governance, and environmental safeguard compliance. Rapid urban growth, transport emissions, and industrial expansion across Africa require robust regulatory enforcement, real-time pollution monitoring, and comprehensive safeguard management.

Participants engage in hands-on exercises covering reference-grade and low-cost sensor networks, dispersion modeling, World Bank ESF / IFC Performance Standards, Environmental & Social Management Plans (ESMPs), and workplace hazard audits.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Environmental Inspectors, NEMA/EPA Regulators, and County/Municipal Air Quality Officers
  • Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE / EHS) Managers in Energy, Manufacturing, and Construction
  • Environmental & Social Safeguard Specialists in World Bank, AfDB, and Donor-Funded Projects
  • EIA/EA Lead Experts, Occupational Hygienists, and Public Health Epidemiologists

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Implement international standards and regulatory compliance protocols for Conducting Environmental Impact Assessment for Projects and Operations.
  • Design and operate ambient and indoor air quality monitoring networks and emissions inventories.
  • Conduct comprehensive Environmental, Social, and Health Impact Assessments (ESIA / EHIA / SEA).
  • Develop and audit Environmental & Social Management Plans (ESMPs) aligned with IFC Performance Standards.
  • Establish ISO 14001 (EMS) and ISO 45001 (OH&S) management systems to prevent workplace incidents and pollution.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: Regulatory Standards, Policy & Governance in Conducting Environmental Impact Assessment for Projects and Operations

  • WHO Air Quality Guidelines, national ambient air & industrial emission tolerance standards, and EHS laws
  • World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and IFC Performance Standards (PS 1–8)
  • Institutional mandates, permitting workflows, and multi-agency compliance enforcement

Module 2: Monitoring Technologies, Baseline Surveys & Risk Assessment

  • Reference-grade analyzers, calibrated low-cost sensor networks, and satellite aerosol optical depth (AOD) data
  • Source apportionment, industrial stack testing, and baseline environmental/health receptor screening
  • Occupational hazard identification, job safety analysis (JSA), and exposure limit monitoring

Module 3: Impact Modeling, Mitigation Hierarchy & Safeguard Instruments

  • Dispersion modeling, cumulative impact analysis, and transboundary risk evaluation
  • Applying the mitigation hierarchy (Avoid, Minimize, Restore, Offset) in infrastructure and energy projects
  • Drafting bankable ESMPs, Stakeholder Engagement Plans (SEPs), and Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GRMs)

Module 4: EMS (ISO 14001), Workplace Safety & Green Operations

  • Implementing ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems and ISO 45001 Occupational Health & Safety
  • Industrial pollution abatement technologies, hazardous waste management, and circular resource use
  • Emergency preparedness, incident investigation (root-cause analysis), and construction site supervision

Module 5: Environmental Auditing, Compliance Reporting & Field Clinic

  • Conducting statutory environmental and safety audits, inspections, and corrective action tracking
  • Health impact economic valuation and public air quality communication indexes (AQI)
  • Practical clinic: Reviewing an ESIA/ESMP or Air Quality Action Plan for regulatory sign-off

consortium-management-and-leadership-tra.title: Consortium Management and Leadership Training
consortium-management-and-leadership-tra.location: Nairobi - Kenya / Mombasa / Arusha / Kigali / Online
consortium-management-and-leadership-tra.summary: This practical executive course on Consortium Management and Leadership Training equips project directors, procurement heads, PPP transaction advisors, and MEAL specialists with rigorous methodologies for project appraisal, public procurement compliance, contract management, donor resource mobilization, and results-based impact evaluation.
consortium-management-and-leadership-tra.content:
OVERVIEW

The Consortium Management and Leadership Training programme is designed to strengthen institutional delivery capacity across complex development programmes, public infrastructure investments, and donor-funded projects. Delays, cost overruns, procurement disputes, and weak monitoring frameworks often undermine project impact; this course provides proven tools to ensure value-for-money, fiduciary compliance, and measurable development outcomes.

Participants engage in practical simulations covering feasibility appraisal, World Bank/national public procurement procedures, Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) PPP structuring, winning grant proposal writing, and Outcome Harvesting / MEAL systems.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Project Directors, Programme Managers, and Project Management Office (PMO) Leads
  • Heads of Procurement, Supply Chain Managers, Tender Committee Members, and Contract Administrators
  • Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) Specialists and Impact Researchers
  • PPP Unit Officers, Infrastructure Transaction Advisors, and Grant/Resource Mobilization Managers

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Apply international standards and operational best practices in Consortium Management and Leadership Training.
  • Conduct rigorous technical, economic, financial, and environmental feasibility appraisals.
  • Manage end-to-end public procurement, competitive bidding, tender evaluation, and FIDIC/NEC contract administration.
  • Structure bankable Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs), Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs), and donor grant proposals.
  • Design Results-Based MEAL frameworks, Theory of Change models, and impact evaluations.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: Strategic Planning, Governance & Legal Frameworks for Consortium Management and Leadership Training

  • Project cycle management (PCM), Theory of Change (ToC), and Logical Framework Approach (LFA)
  • Public procurement statutes, World Bank/AfDB procurement regulations, and PPP legal frameworks
  • Stakeholder mapping, consortium governance, and institutional risk allocation matrices

Module 2: Feasibility Analysis, Appraisal & Resource Mobilization

  • Technical, financial, economic (ERR/NPV), and social/environmental appraisal of projects
  • Structuring Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs), concession agreements, and blended project finance
  • Donor intelligence, competitive grant proposal writing, and financial sustainability planning

Module 3: Procurement Planning, Tendering & Contract Management

  • Strategic procurement planning, drafting standard bidding documents (SBDs), and Terms of Reference (ToRs)
  • Bid evaluation methodologies, value-for-money analysis, and contract negotiation techniques
  • Contract administration, variation management, SLA monitoring, and dispute resolution

Module 4: Results-Based MEAL, Safeguards & Performance Contracting

  • Designing KPI indicator matrices, baseline surveys, and Outcome Harvesting methodologies
  • Social safeguards, involuntary resettlement action plans (RAP), and rights-based project delivery
  • Earned Value Management (EVM), project restructuring, and turnaround of stalled projects

Module 5: Audit Readiness, Impact Evaluation & Capstone Clinic

  • Counterfactual impact evaluation (RCTs, quasi-experimental designs) and value-for-money audits
  • Preventing procurement fraud, collusion, and audit queries in public and donor projects
  • Capstone workshop: Developing a complete Procurement Plan, PPP Term Sheet, or MEAL Framework

evaluation-and-impact-assessment-of-poli.title: Evaluation and Impact Assessment of Policies and Projects
evaluation-and-impact-assessment-of-poli.location: Nairobi - Kenya / Mombasa / Arusha / Kigali / Online
evaluation-and-impact-assessment-of-poli.summary: This technical executive course on Evaluation and Impact Assessment of Policies and Projects equips environmental regulators, EHS managers, urban planners, and infrastructure safeguard specialists with practical methodologies for air quality monitoring, industrial emissions control, Environmental & Social Impact Assessments (ESIA), and ISO 14001/45001 compliance.
evaluation-and-impact-assessment-of-poli.content:
OVERVIEW

The Evaluation and Impact Assessment of Policies and Projects training programme provides rigorous, practitioner-focused instruction on environmental protection, occupational health and safety (HSE), urban air quality governance, and environmental safeguard compliance. Rapid urban growth, transport emissions, and industrial expansion across Africa require robust regulatory enforcement, real-time pollution monitoring, and comprehensive safeguard management.

Participants engage in hands-on exercises covering reference-grade and low-cost sensor networks, dispersion modeling, World Bank ESF / IFC Performance Standards, Environmental & Social Management Plans (ESMPs), and workplace hazard audits.

TARGET PARTICIPANTS

  • Environmental Inspectors, NEMA/EPA Regulators, and County/Municipal Air Quality Officers
  • Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE / EHS) Managers in Energy, Manufacturing, and Construction
  • Environmental & Social Safeguard Specialists in World Bank, AfDB, and Donor-Funded Projects
  • EIA/EA Lead Experts, Occupational Hygienists, and Public Health Epidemiologists

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

  • Implement international standards and regulatory compliance protocols for Evaluation and Impact Assessment of Policies and Projects.
  • Design and operate ambient and indoor air quality monitoring networks and emissions inventories.
  • Conduct comprehensive Environmental, Social, and Health Impact Assessments (ESIA / EHIA / SEA).
  • Develop and audit Environmental & Social Management Plans (ESMPs) aligned with IFC Performance Standards.
  • Establish ISO 14001 (EMS) and ISO 45001 (OH&S) management systems to prevent workplace incidents and pollution.

COURSE OUTLINE

Module 1: Regulatory Standards, Policy & Governance in Evaluation and Impact Assessment of Policies and Projects

  • WHO Air Quality Guidelines, national ambient air & industrial emission tolerance standards, and EHS laws
  • World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and IFC Performance Standards (PS 1–8)
  • Institutional mandates, permitting workflows, and multi-agency compliance enforcement

Module 2: Monitoring Technologies, Baseline Surveys & Risk Assessment

  • Reference-grade analyzers, calibrated low-cost sensor networks, and satellite aerosol optical depth (AOD) data
  • Source apportionment, industrial stack testing, and baseline environmental/health receptor screening
  • Occupational hazard identification, job safety analysis (JSA), and exposure limit monitoring

Module 3: Impact Modeling, Mitigation Hierarchy & Safeguard Instruments

  • Dispersion modeling, cumulative impact analysis, and transboundary risk evaluation
  • Applying the mitigation hierarchy (Avoid, Minimize, Restore, Offset) in infrastructure and energy projects
  • Drafting bankable ESMPs, Stakeholder Engagement Plans (SEPs), and Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GRMs)

Module 4: EMS (ISO 14001), Workplace Safety & Green Operations

  • Implementing ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems and ISO 45001 Occupational Health & Safety
  • Industrial pollution abatement technologies, hazardous waste management, and circular resource use
  • Emergency preparedness, incident investigation (root-cause analysis), and construction site supervision

Module 5: Environmental Auditing, Compliance Reporting & Field Clinic

  • Conducting statutory environmental and safety audits, inspections, and corrective action tracking
  • Health impact economic valuation and public air quality communication indexes (AQI)
  • Practical clinic: Reviewing an ESIA/ESMP or Air Quality Action Plan for regulatory sign-off
